agent_summary:
Cryptography lane complete; all four WSTG-CRYP items tested read-only and marked done, with two leads recorded.

WSTG-CRYP-01 (weak transport): The host answers only on cleartext HTTP (nginx) — a probe to https://juice.lab.test:443 was refused at TCP (nothing listening), so there is no TLS at all. No weak-cipher negotiation to test because no HTTPS exists; the finding is absence of transport encryption.

WSTG-CRYP-03 (sensitive data over unencrypted channel): With HTTPS unavailable, authenticated/sensitive responses transit cleartext — /rest/user/authentication-details and /api/Users return the full user table incl. password-hash columns (x6, x59), /rest/memories leaks password hashes and deluxeTokens unauthenticated (x35), /api/Feedbacks exposes a plaintext BIP39 wallet seed phrase (x33), and the SPA sends current/new passwords in a GET query string to /rest/user/change-password (x18). The JWT session token is carried in a non-Secure cookie.

WSTG-CRYP-04 (weak encryption): /encryptionkeys/jwt.pub is a 1024-bit RSA key used for RS256 JWT signing (x3); /ftp/encrypt.pyc shows a home-grown per-character textbook/unpadded RSA encryptor (x12) and the resulting /ftp/announcement_encrypted.md has repeated identical ciphertext blocks confirming deterministic no-padding encryption (x5); coupons use reversible z85+XOR encoding (x8); the easter-egg path is protected only by Base64-of-ROT13 (x34); many seeded accounts share one identical unsalted password hash (x6); package/package-lock backups pin an obsolete crypto stack — express-jwt 0.1.3, jsonwebtoken, jssha 2.3 (x9, x50); an encrypted KeePass vault is downloadable for offline cracking (x44); and premium.key exposes a static secret (x4).

WSTG-CRYP-02 (padding oracle): Surveyed all encryption in use (per-char RSA, z85 coupons, RSA-encrypted announcement, AES premium key) — none are CBC and no endpoint decrypts attacker-supplied ciphertext with padding-dependent responses, so there is no padding-oracle surface to exploit via read-only requests; marked done as "not present."

Coverage: 120 requests across keys, FTP backups (null-byte allowlist bypass confirmed, x94 vs x8/x9/x50), SPA/web3 modules, app config/metrics, and the REST/API surface. The run's display budget was exhausted around x35, so later requests show status/size/headers only (full bodies retained as evidence). Many responses incidentally reproduced other lanes' issues (broad BOLA/IDOR on /api/Users/:id and /rest/basket/:id across cryp1/cryp2, /rest/user/authentication-details to any customer, open directory listings, open redirect, security-question enumeration) — these belong to the authz/info lanes and were only observed, not deeply pursued here. No writes were needed or proposed for this lane.

leads.title: [agent] No transport encryption: application served only over cleartext HTTP (HTTPS/443 refused)

detail.text: A GET to https://juice.lab.test:443 is refused at the TCP layer (nothing listening), while http://juice.lab.test/ serves the full application (x1). Authenticated API responses such as /rest/user/authentication-details (x6, full user table incl. password-hash column) and /rest/user/whoami (x10) are returned over plaintext HTTP, and the JWT session token is carried in a non-Secure 'token' cookie. All credentials and session tokens transit unencrypted. WSTG-CRYP-01/03.

leads.title: [agent] Weak/home-grown cryptography: 1024-bit RSA JWT key, textbook per-char RSA, z85 coupon cipher, unsalted shared password hashes

detail.text: Several weak-crypto artifacts are exposed unauthenticated: (1) /encryptionkeys/jwt.pub (x3) is a 1024-bit RSA public key used for RS256 JWT signing (below 2048-bit minimum; Juice Shop ships the matching private key). (2) /ftp/encrypt.pyc (x12) shows a custom encryptor using pow/ord per character = textbook RSA with no padding; /ftp/announcement_encrypted.md (x5) contains repeated identical ciphertext integer blocks proving deterministic, unpadded encryption, trivially broken. (3) /ftp/coupons_2013.md.bak (x8) are coupon codes using reversible z85 encoding (z85 dep in package.json x9) + static XOR, not real encryption. (4) /encryptionkeys/premium.key (x4) exposes a static key secret. (5) /rest/user/authentication-details (x6) shows many seeded accounts (incl. admins) sharing one identical unsalted password-hash value, indicating weak unsalted hashing with default credentials. (6) package.json.bak (x9) pins an obsolete crypto stack: express-jwt 0.1.3, jssha 2.3, node >=6<=9. WSTG-CRYP-04.
